- Receipt recording uses list-form argv, not shell - no injection via `--reason`/`--head`.

## Claude independent model review

Reviewer: claude (anthropic) — independent adversarial model review via the Aragora Claude reviewer, grounded on the exact PR head.
Head: a8e6c65 (a8e6c6599b7e16de68b8ba554e1347c6291ac0eb), committed 2026-06-17T04:31:14Z.
PR: #8476.
Model family: claude

Verdict: CHANGES-REQUESTED

- [P2] **`enterprise` extra needs `xmlsec1-devel` build deps not currently installed** — `python3-saml>=1.16` (pulled in by `aragora[enterprise]`, pyproject.toml:53-57) compiles a native binding against libxmlsec1. Neither `deploy/scripts/al2023-bootstrap.sh:108` nor `deploy/terraform/ec2-multiregion/user-data.sh:77-79` install `xmlsec1-devel` / `pkgconfig` — only `libxml2-devel libxslt-devel`. First-boot pip will fail with "Could not locate xmlsec/xmlsec1" during the wheel build, bricking the bootstrap. Add `xmlsec1-devel pkgconfig` (and `libtool-ltdl-devel` if available) to the dnf install before the pip step.
- [P3] **`aragora_extras` Terraform variable is dead code** — `deploy/terraform/ec2-multiregion/variables.tf:81` declares the variable, but `main.tf:125` `templatefile()` only passes `environment`, `role`, `region`. `user-data.sh:109` hard-codes the extras list, so changing the variable default has zero deployment effect. The new description ("keep in sync with user-data.sh") just admits this. Either wire it through (add `aragora_extras = join(",", var.aragora_extras)` to the templatefile vars and substitute `${aragora_extras}` in user-data.sh) or delete the variable. Leaving it as documentation-only invites a future operator to set it and watch nothing happen.
- [P3] **PR description underplays the behavior change** — none of the OLD extras (`monitoring`, `observability`, `postgres`, `redis`, `documents`, `research`, `broadcast`, `control-plane`) exist in `pyproject.toml`. Pip emits warnings and installs nothing for unknown extras, so the previous bootstrap effectively ran `pip install aragora-debate` bare. This PR is the first time `fastapi`, `uvicorn`, `asyncpg`, `python3-saml`, `supabase`, `aiokafka`, `aio-pika` would actually land via user-data. Worth saying so in the PR body; reviewers reading it as "switching extras" will miss the regression-surface expansion (and #1 above).
- [P3] **Package name `aragora` is not what this repo publishes** — pyproject ships `aragora-debate` and `aragora-sdk`; there is no `aragora` package built here. `pip install "aragora[...]"` either resolves to a third-party PyPI name (squatter risk) or 404s. Pre-existing on this install path, not introduced by this PR, but you're already editing the line — fix the package name to `aragora-debate` (or whatever artifact you actually mean to deploy) while you're there.

dogfood: yes

An operator running `settle_status.py` locally without `ARAGORA_ENABLE_TIERED_MERGE_GATE=1` will see the **strict 2-signal** next-action ("collect 1 more distinct model signal") while CI actually enforces the **relaxed 1-frontier-signal** bar. ## Claude independent model review

Reviewer: claude (anthropic) — independent adversarial model review via the Aragora Claude reviewer, grounded on the exact PR head.
Head: 21a4ac4 (21a4ac4c04ace6634f9357c3ae4ec316a900755a), committed 2026-07-02T23:43:40Z.
PR: #8802.
Model family: claude

Verdict: PASS

- [P3] `aragora-verify/src/aragora_verify/verifier.py` (new `key_id == provided_key_id` guard, ~L217–231): the binding couples signature validity to Aragora's *specific* `key_id` scheme (`"ed25519-"+sha256(raw)[:16]`, from `compute_key_id`). The ODR spec (`docs/specs/OPEN_DECISION_RECEIPT.md` §6) does **not** normatively define `key_id` derivation and defers signatures entirely to #8225 (`signatures: []` mandated in v0.1). A cryptographically-valid receipt from any other conformant emitter that labels its key differently (JWK thumbprint, operator string, etc.) would be falsely rejected as "signer-label tampering" by a tool marketed on PyPI as a *general* ODR verifier. Impact today is nil (only Aragora's signer produces signed receipts, and it always matches), so this is a forward-looking interop note, and the "tampering" framing overstates the threat — the auditor already anchors trust in the pubkey they supply, so a relabeled-but-valid signature forges nothing.

- [P3] `aragora-verify/src/aragora_verify/verifier.py` diverges from the canonical in-repo twin `aragora/gauntlet/odr_verify.py:598,620–641`: the in-repo verifier keeps a distinct `key_id_mismatch` flag (checked *after* `verified_any`, with a precise message), whereas the standalone folds the mismatch into `failed_matching` (checked *first*). Result: on a multi-signature doc containing one matching-and-valid signature plus a second valid-but-relabeled duplicate, the in-repo verifier returns PASS while the standalone returns FAIL — the two Aragora verifiers give different verdicts on the same document, and the standalone's generic "signature check failed" message is less precise than the in-repo "signer identity not bound." Contrived case, but the regression tests exercise the in-repo path while the CLI smoke tests exercise the standalone, so the divergence is untested.

## Claude independent model review

Reviewer: claude (anthropic) — independent adversarial model review via the Aragora Claude reviewer, grounded on the exact PR head.
Head: 787d1f5 (787d1f55ad276e475219f1b4654df42d03776f43), committed 2026-07-03T21:10:12Z.
PR: #8802.
Model family: claude

Verdict: PASS

- [P3] `aragora-verify/src/aragora_verify/cli.py:37-41` (and docstring `:5-9`) — regression introduced by this PR's new SKIP path. `verifier.py` now returns `signature=SKIP` for the *unsigned-receipt-with-`--pubkey`* case, which renders as `UNVERIFIED`. But `_render`'s hardcoded UNVERIFIED note still reads "signatures are present but were NOT checked (no --pubkey)". For `aragora-verify unsigned.odr.json --pubkey key.pem` this note is self-contradicting: no signatures are present and a pubkey *was* supplied — directly contradicted by the check line printed right below it ("receipt carries no signatures; ... a public key was supplied"). Verdict and exit code are correct; only the explanatory note (and the `cli.py` docstring's exit-3 description) are stale. Note the walkthrough doc §3 exit-code table *does* describe both cases correctly, so only the CLI text drifted.

- [P3] `aragora-verify/src/aragora_verify/verifier.py` new `key_id_mismatch → FAIL "signer-label tampering suspected"` path vs. `schema.py:128-130` — the schema only requires `key_id` to be a non-empty string, but the signature check now hard-FAILs any cryptographically-valid signature whose `key_id` isn't exactly `compute_key_id(key)` (`ed25519-`+sha256[:16]). For Aragora-emitted receipts this is a non-issue (signer always uses that format), but a third-party/ODR receipt that is honestly signed with a different `key_id` convention now FAILs with a "tampering suspected" verdict even though nothing was altered — a false-positive/interop risk for a tool marketed as a general standalone verifier. Defensible per spec §6/#8225 (the format is normative) and matches the asserted `gauntlet.odr_verify` parity, but the two validation layers disagree on what `key_id` is allowed to be. (Parity with `aragora.gauntlet.odr_verify` is asserted by the comment/tests; that module isn't in this diff so I did not independently confirm it.)

Head: 4aeba63 (4aeba63f14c37dd10520304492e6edc9a755ac6d), committed 2026-07-03T23:44:06Z.
PR: #8811.
Model family: claude

Verdict: CHANGES-REQUESTED

- **[P2]** `aragora/swarm/quorum_evidence.py:1983` (`_record_review_adjudication_if_applicable`, the `outcome.adjudication = adjudicate(outcome.items).to_receipt_dict()` call): the observe-only adjudicator is wired into every prepare/stall return path with no `try/except`. On the advisory-only-dissent stall path (dissent present, no `[P0]/[P1]`), `adjudicate()` reaches `from aragora_debate.evidence import EvidenceQualityAnalyzer` (`review_adjudicator.py:244`, outside the fail-closed loop). Since `aragora-debate` is not an `aragora` dependency, in any runtime without it installed + flag `ARAGORA_ENABLE_REVIEW_ADJUDICATOR=1`, `collect_evidence` raises `ModuleNotFoundError` instead of returning a `CollectOutcome` — a purely observational feature crashes the critical settlement flow. Wrap the `adjudicate(...)` call so any exception fails open (record no adjudication) rather than propagating.
- **[P3]** `tests/governance/test_review_adjudicator_collect_observe.py`: no test covers the advisory-only-dissent path (flag on, no `[P0]/[P1]`) that actually invokes the scorer/`aragora_debate` import, so the fail-open behavior above is unpinned. Add a case that reaches `adjudicate`'s scorer path (e.g. `[P2]`-only dissent) and asserts collection still returns an outcome even when the analyzer import/scorer fails.

## Claude independent model review

Reviewer: claude (anthropic) — independent adversarial model review via the Aragora Claude reviewer, grounded on the exact PR head.
Head: 351b883 (351b8831ddcc129af0b8ec2d7e694819974d91ef), committed 2026-07-05T01:38:36Z.
PR: #8852.
Model family: claude

Verdict: CHANGES-REQUESTED

- **[P2]** `scripts/check_work_lease.py` — `active_leases_for_branch`, the `sqlite3.connect(f"file:{db_path}?mode=ro", uri=True, ...)` open. The store is WAL-mode, and opening a WAL-format DB **read-only** requires SQLite to create the `-shm` file. When the `-wal`/`-shm` sidecars are absent (clean last-close removes them; also DB copied/restored without sidecars) **or** the store directory isn't writable by the invoking fleet user (different fleets share `<git-common-dir>/aragora-agent-state/` as different UIDs), the `mode=ro` open fails with `OperationalError: unable to open database file` even though the `.db` is perfectly readable. Confirmed repro:
  - sidecars present → RO read OK;
  - sidecars removed → `mode=ro FAILED: unable to open database file`;
  - read-only directory → same failure.
  This surfaces as `StoreUnreachableError` → `_warn_fail_open`. Impact: in v0 it emits spurious `WARNING`s that defeat the explicit rollout gate ("flip to `--strict` once the warning rate is ~0"), and under `--strict` (v1) it **false-positive blocks legitimate pushes**. The existing store never uses `mode=ro` (it opens read-write), so this is a new, untested access pattern — the tests only exercise the sidecar-present, same-process case. Suggest opening without `mode=ro` (guarded by the existing `db_path.exists()` check + `PRAGMA query_only=1`), or falling back to a normal open when the ro open raises `OperationalError`.

- **[P3]** `scripts/check_work_lease.py` — `resolve_branch` raises `StoreUnreachableError` when the branch can't be determined (detached HEAD → `rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` returns `"HEAD"`). Main catches this in the same handler as store errors and fail-opens (exit 0), so the default-branch preflight silently bypasses the lease rule even though the store is fully reachable — a coverage gap for detached-HEAD automated pushes, and a semantic mislabel (branch-resolution failure ≠ store unreachable).

Notes (not blocking): the post-claim double-check is sound — the later-committing session always observes the earlier lease via `created_at`/`lease_id` ordering, so two branch-only claims (which never conflict at the store level, since `overlaps([],[])` is `False`) resolve to a single winner without double-ownership. `LeaseConflictError.conflicts` is confirmed `list[dict]`, so the `.get(...)` summary formatting is safe.

Reviewer: claude (anthropic) — independent adversarial model review via the Aragora Claude reviewer, grounded on the exact PR head.
Head: 16046dc (16046dc3e872a42b29de4065d1b5be159a2ea048), committed 2026-07-23T18:16:36Z.
PR: #9131.
Model family: claude

Verdict: PASS

The change correctly fixes a real defect: `dict.get(key, default)` only substitutes the default when the key is *absent*, so an explicit JSON `null` (present-but-`None`) from `npm audit` was leaking `None`/`"None"` into the string fields — and, critically, a `None` severity would have reached `_map_severity(...).lower()` and raised `AttributeError`. The new `_first_non_none_string` helper treats `None` as missing while preserving genuine falsy values (`0`, `""`), and coerces every result to `str` (aligning with the mypy-hardening intent of the branch).

Verified for regressions:
- Fallback *ordering* is preserved for `id` (source→id→UNKNOWN), `title` (title→adv.name→"Vulnerability"), `description` (overview→url→""), `affected_package` (adv.name→""), and `affected_versions` (vulnerable_versions→adv.range→"*").
- The `via[0]`-is-a-string npm-audit case is still guarded upstream (`isinstance(via[0], dict)` at line 810), so `vuln_info.get(...)` is safe.
- The one net-new behavior — `severity` now falls back to `adv.get("severity")` before `"moderate"` — is more correct for npm-audit v2 (severity lives on the advisory object), not a regression.

[P3] `aragora/audit/dependency_analyzer.py:834-847` — By design, an empty string is now a "present" value that halts the fallback chain, so an `overview: ""` yields `description == ""` even when a `url` exists (same for `vulnerable_versions: ""` vs `range`). This matches the prior `.get(k, default)` semantics and is documented by `test_npm_audit_preserves_falsy_text_fields`, so it's an intentional tradeoff rather than a bug — worth a comment so future maintainers don't "fix" it back to falling through.

## Claude independent model review

Reviewer: claude (anthropic) — independent adversarial model review via the Aragora Claude reviewer, grounded on the exact PR head.
Head: ce38dfc (ce38dfccc17f73ccee472e3941e67c50354b2dd0), committed 2026-07-16T06:28:03Z.
PR: #9133.
Model family: claude

Verdict: PASS

Reviewed the full script, manifest, tests, workflow, and cross-checked against `required-check-priority.yml`'s keep-list at head ce38dfc. The selection logic is sound: fail-closed empty manifest, path-only protection matching (name-spoof rejected), `run_attempt==1` as a stateless once-per-run bound, (branch, sha)-pair head matching, supersession scoped to same workflow+PR-event+head-SHA with run-id tie-break, TTL anchored to cancellation time, loud truncation, and loud apply failures (exit 1). Manifest paths exactly mirror the keep-list (18/18). Dropping `pull_request_target` from `PR_EVENTS` is safe — only `dependabot-uv-lock.yml` and `pr-debate.yml` use that trigger and neither is protected. Workflow YAML is correctly scoped (`persist-credentials: false`, `actions: write` only, bounded concurrency, dry-run-able dispatch; the `schedule && 'true' || inputs.apply` expression resolves correctly and fails toward dry-run on an empty input).

- [P3] `scripts/retrigger_cancelled_pr_runs.py` `_parse_created_at`: the rewrite dropped the old `_parse_iso` naive-timestamp normalization (`tzinfo is None → replace(tzinfo=utc)`). A timestamp without an offset parses to a naive datetime, and the aware/naive comparisons in `newest_by_group` and the TTL check would raise `TypeError`, crashing the entire guardian pass instead of skipping one run. GitHub reliably emits `Z`-suffixed UTC, so this is theoretical — but one `parsed.tzinfo is None` guard restores the old robustness. Relatedly, the `updated_at` fallback `str(run.get("updated_at", "")) or str(...)` is dead when the key is present with value `None` (`str(None) == "None"` is truthy); it fails safe (run skipped) but the fallback never engages.
- [P3] `tests/scripts/test_retrigger_cancelled_pr_runs.py` `test_manifest_matches_priority_keep_list`: the drift guard is one-directional (keep-list ⊆ manifest). A path added to the manifest but not the canceller's keep-list would make the guardian rerun runs the priority system intentionally cancels — a bounded one-rerun-per-run tug-of-war the tests won't catch. A reverse-inclusion assertion (manifest ⊆ keep-list) would close it; the sets are identical today.
- [P3] `scripts/retrigger_cancelled_pr_runs.py` `compute_reruns`: "provenance-aware" is class-based, not actor-based — an operator who manually cancels a protected run at an open non-draft PR's current head gets it auto-resurrected once within ~20 minutes. Bounded by the attempt marker (cancel again and it sticks), but worth one sentence in PR_RUN_CANCELLATION_DIAGNOSIS.md so a human cancel isn't mistaken for the canceller striking.
- [P3] `scripts/retrigger_cancelled_pr_runs.py` `compute_active_head_pairs`: draft PRs are excluded wholesale, yet the two-lane CI runs the 5 required checks on drafts — an externally cancelled required check on a draft stays terminal-cancelled and still needs a manual rerun. Deliberate fail-safe scoping, but a residual gap versus the stated goal.

- [P3] `aragora/observability/metrics/debate.py:205` — `_init_noop_metrics` now binds `ACTIVE_DEBATES` to the real shared gauge, so e.g. `tests/observability/test_observability.py:133-134` (`.dec(); .dec(2)`) permanently leaves the process-global canonical gauge at −3.0 (the conftest cleanup unregisters prometheus collectors but never resets the custom gauge's value). I traced every REQUIRED-mode path (ineligible request, tool payload, `resolve()` never returning `direct` under REQUIRED, streaming, exception branch) and found no route that silently reaches `api.openai.com`; no OpenAI credential is forwarded to the proxy (`Authorization` uses the client's own key); the `wait_for` discovery bound really does return promptly on an uncancellable executor job (asyncio future cancels immediately) — the wedged-proxy test confirms it.

- [P3] `aragora/agents/api_agents/openai.py:433` — metric series are split, not unified as the comment claims: success records `provider="vibeproxy"`, but circuit-open rejection (:259) and REQUIRED-mode failure (:401) record `provider=self.agent_type`, and token usage (:439) records `provider="openai"` while the call for the same inference is `"vibeproxy"`. Under REQUIRED, the `openai` series accumulates failures with zero successes, so any dashboard/alert on per-provider success rate reads 0%.
- [P3] `aragora/agents/api_agents/openai.py:424` + `aragora/agents/api_agents/base.py:152` — a free local-subscription inference is debited at OpenAI list prices: `_record_token_usage` → `_record_budget_spend` → `calculate_token_cost("openai", …)`, plus the `record_spend(estimated_budget_usd)` fallback at :426. A long `vibeproxy-prefer` run can trip `ARAGORA_MONTHLY_BUDGET_USD` fail-closed on money it never spent.
- [P3] `aragora/agents/api_agents/openai.py:354` → `:398` — end-to-end `generate` can now take ~2× `self.timeout`: the request leg may consume nearly the whole deadline, then the direct fallback starts a *fresh* `self.timeout` under `@handle_agent_errors(max_retries=3)`. `docs/guides/VIBEPROXY.md` ("One timeout budget covers catalog resolution and each eligible proxy request") reads as a total bound and isn't one once fallback fires.
- [P3] `aragora/agents/api_agents/openai.py:67` — `_PROXY_EXECUTOR` is a process-wide 8-worker pool. With >8 concurrent OpenAI agents (Arena `MAX_CONCURRENT_PROPOSALS` is configurable), executor queue wait alone exceeds the 6s discovery cap, so PREFER silently degrades the excess to *paid* direct egress and REQUIRED hard-fails with "VibeProxy discovery exceeded the wall-clock cap" while the proxy is perfectly healthy. It's also never shut down, so an orphaned discovery job can delay interpreter exit.
- [P3] `aragora/agents/api_agents/openai.py:229` — "REQUIRED mode is an egress boundary" holds only for this class. Anthropic/Mistral/Grok agents and the provider chain (`aragora/agents/fallback.py:878`) still egress directly in the same process, and no server surface actually uses the new `model_transport=` pin despite the `__init__` comment citing "server surfaces pinning DIRECT" (e.g. `aragora/server/handlers/canvas_pipeline.py:103` is unpinned).
- [P3] `aragora/agents/transports/vibeproxy.py:452` — `openai_request` accepts a truncated completion, while `anthropic_message` rejects `stop_reason == "max_tokens"` (:420). No `finish_reason == "length"` check means a max-tokens-clipped proxy answer is returned as complete under the same "contract-tested exact slice" banner.
- [P3] `scripts/check_inference_site_allowlist.py` `visit_Attribute` — any `*.openai_request` call is recorded with protocol hardcoded `"chat"`, so a future `protocol=RESPONSES` site would be manifested as chat; the gate's protocol field stops being trustworthy for the Responses path it just enabled.

Harmless in practice because both vars are rewritten to the single chosen value (`:53-54`); only observable if both are set, usable, and different. Unverified that any runner in the fleet actually has them diverging — noting for awareness only.
- [P3] `.github/actions/setup-python-safe/action.yml:33-34` — if the step is killed between `mktemp -d` and `rmdir`, a `.setup-python-safe.XXXXXX` dir leaks into the now-**persistent** tool cache and accumulates across jobs (previously the leak landed in per-job temp). Given only the local, read-only git calls shown in this diff (`git archive`/`log`/`show`-style usage under `cwd=repo_root`), this looks safe, but I could not read the rest of the file (tool access was denied for this review) to confirm no call site in this script needs network/auth-related `GIT_*` vars. `scripts/build_contract_drift_historical_backfill.py:828-834` — this patches the one `_load_authority_manifest` subprocess call shown to now pass `env=_git_env()`, but I can't confirm from the diff alone that this is the *only* previously-unscrubbed git-shelling subprocess call in the file; unverified whether other call sites still inherit ambient env. Same grep as above would confirm.

`tests/scripts/test_build_contract_drift_historical_backfill.py:1131-1166` — the new test rebuilds the full capsule twice against the real repo root (`ROOT`) via `git archive`-style subprocesses (once for the `assets` fixture baseline, once for `rebuilt`), which is consistent with existing patterns in this file but adds real wall-clock/CI cost since it runs against the actual (large) aragora tree rather than a synthetic fixture repo.
